title: Carl Pawel to Frederick V, King of Bohemia, 25 Nov 1624 (BSB Clm 10382 n. 46): the letter cipher is the casimir1629 alphabet moved by 3, rebuilt from the contemporary glosses and tested on a held-out page

documents.shelfmark: Munich, Bayerische Staatsbibliothek, Clm 10382 (Collectio Camerariana 32), n. 46 (MDZ bsb00112117, scans 181-182)
documents.route: Carl Pawel -> Frederick V, King of Bohemia (Elector Palatine in exile)

plaintext.source: A contemporary decipherment is written above the code groups and the letter runs (Halm 1874 p. 59: 'in Chiffern mit Auflösungen').

transcription.source: MDZ bsb00112117 scans 181-182 (microfilm, 1334 px, Public Domain Mark 1.0)
transcription.notes: The 17 runs of two-digit numbers (letters) with their glosses only. The 3-4 digit code groups, the signs and the clear German text are not transcribed. Scan 181 = training, scan 182 = held out.

system.summary: Mixed: a code of 3-4 digit numbers for words and names (2737 Ob. Fuchs, 3515 Stuttgart, 2224 kommen, 1732 Mansfelt, 2389 Liga), a few signs (a3 = zu, mm = so, rr = und), and a German letter cipher written as comma-separated two-digit numbers, with homophones in blocks of three: 11-13 a, 14-16 g, 17-19 n, 20-22 t, 23-25 b, 26-28 h, 29-31 o, 32-34 u/v, 35-37 c, 38-40 i, 41-43 p, 44-46 w, 47-49 d, 50-52 k, 56-58 x, 59-61 e, 62-64 l, 65-67 r, 68-70 y, 71-73 f, 74-76 m, 77-79 s, 80-82 z. This is the casimir1629 letter alphabet with every number lowered by 3.

prior_solution.where: The contemporary interlinear decipherment on the letter (Halm 1874 p. 59, 'in Chiffern mit Auflösungen'); leads review batch b70 (4 Nov 2026) found every group glossed and closed lead 2179 as 'read', noting it as a key source with no key built. No edition found; not on DECODE; no target, PR or issue for Pawel or Clm 10382 n. 46 in this repository (GitHub API, origin/main e4c7843d, 5 Nov 2026).

conditions.human_role: Daniel Bourdeau's leads review (batch b70) located and vetted the piece as lead 2179. Brice Dudout set the rules (protocol and key frozen by SHA-256 before a single held-out measurement, thresholds fixed in advance). AI agents transcribed, tested the casimir1629 key, measured and wrote up. No human palaeographer checked the transcription.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout

solution.what: Scan 181: 15 runs of two-digit numbers with their interlinear glosses, transcribed by eye from the microfilm.

The frozen casimir1629 key was tried with every shift from -12 to 12 on the glossed runs of scan 181; a shift of 3 gives 0.921 (next best 0.737). Gaps filled from scan 181, blocks of three; frozen by SHA-256 with the protocol before scan 182 was looked at.

One measurement on scan 182, transcribed after the freeze: 2 glossed runs, 13 letters. Score 1.000 (whole words 1.000) against 0.154 for the best of 200 shuffled keys; thresholds >= 0.85 and >= 0.30 above the best control, fixed in advance. The held-out part is very small.
The only unglossed run, 16 59 66 38 20 22 60 17 on scan 181, reads 'geritten' ('zu ruck geritten'), where the glossator wrote 'zu rückh kommen'.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key is the casimir1629 alphabet moved by 3; the shift was fitted on the contemporary glosses of scan 181 and validated once on scan 182. The content is the glosses' (existing); the key, the shared system and one unglossed run are the contribution.

validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered held-out test (not docs/_validate.py): protocol and key hashed before scan 182 was looked at; one measurement on scan 182 (2 glossed runs, 13 letters): 1.000 vs best of 200 shuffled keys 0.154. Thresholds fixed in advance: >= 0.85 and >= 0.30 above the best control. Limit: the held-out part has only 13 letters. Two numbers on scan 181 (181.14, 181.15) were re-read after the measurement; the key did not change.

texts.label: n. 46 (scans 181-182): letter runs with their contemporary glosses
texts.note: A word list, not a running text: each run of two-digit numbers with the gloss written above it at the time and our decode with key.tsv. The code groups and the clear text are not transcribed.
texts.summary: Carl Pawel reports to Frederick V on Colonel Fuchs's recruiting in Württemberg: Fuchs came to Stuttgart and stayed until Tuesday the 23rd, accompanied; the letter speaks of the 'pars victrix', of someone who 'rode back', of Mansfeld and the League, and of men who could be used.

reading_review.note: Word list checked against the contemporary glosses, letter by letter; not prose, clear text not transcribed.
reading_review.by: Claude Opus 5.5 agent for Brice Dudout

outcome.notes: The letter was deciphered at the time (interlinear glosses), so we claim no reading and no solution. New: the letter key as a reusable table; the finding that it is the casimir1629 alphabet moved by 3 (a family of Palatine keys with a movable origin); and one unglossed run read.
